scope: Implementation-phase Work audit: every one of50 bullets and nine phase gates in plan section11. Sections1–10,12–17 and the named test sets require their own invariant/compatibility/maintenance/release reviews; this is not the complete plan audit or release qualification. A supported work item means the cited implementation/evidence supports its stated assessment, not unrestricted proof of every possible execution.

phases.heading: F0 — Capture the 0.4.0 baseline (must precede refactoring)

work_items.requirement: Record release tag `v0.4.0` and HEAD SHA, toolchain versions, host characteristics, `cargo metadata`, public API exports, current feature matrix, release crate list and existing protocol golden fixtures.
work_items.assessment: Original tag/commit, toolchains, metadata, feature inventory and source hashes are frozen; later candidate evidence has a distinct source scope.

work_items.requirement: Run the existing workspace/MSRV/portable/CI-equivalent checks, full selected chaos/fuzz/coverage profiles, current saga/task/timeline examples, and representative performance benches.
work_items.assessment: Baseline checks and completed default chaos exist on unchanged original source, with equivalent-work comparisons. This audit does not prove every profile finished before implementation began; performance conclusions also remain open.

work_items.requirement: Record any failing pre-existing test, expected latency exception, nondeterminism, or environment limitation as an explicit baseline deviation. Do **not** erase a failing test just to make 0.5 appear green.
work_items.assessment: Original advisory failures, interrupted campaign and environment limitations remain recorded; completed unchanged-source chaos supplements the interrupted attempt.

work_items.requirement: Create a dependency/semantics map for `penelope-core`, `domain`, `executor`, `ports`, `sqlite`, `timeline`, and `process-runtime`, including all public reexports that downstream users may import.
work_items.assessment: Baseline semantics map and facade snapshot describe old ownership; independent export traversal reviews retained bindings across14 profiles.

work_items.requirement: Freeze copies of old protocol test fixtures and a baseline API compile harness as external sample crates.
work_items.assessment: Independent consumer and frozen old task/timeline/saga observations are retained, with an actual old-writer database fixture.

phases.gate: Baseline is command-reproducible, limitations are recorded, and old-version fixtures can be checked against new code in later phases.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

phases.heading: F1 — Define unified contracts and compatibility policy

work_items.requirement: Approve the state/event/transition, guard, rejection, HSM, intent, prepared-candidate and commit life cycles from sections 3–7.
work_items.assessment: ADRs settle reducer, hierarchy, consuming publication, separate storage authority and native engine boundaries; API sketches in the imported plan are not presented as compiled API.

work_items.requirement: Define the precise distinctions between `Rejected`, `Unhandled`, evaluation fault, conflict, durable commit ambiguity and effect ambiguity.
work_items.assessment: Rejected/unhandled do not publish; evaluation errors preserve concrete types. CAS conflict, missing commit acknowledgement and unknown external effect remain separate contracts.

work_items.requirement: Specify `MachineScope`, definition fingerprint, schema identity, accepted event IDs, sequence/revision, stable transition identity and provenance view, with no unsafe implicit conversions from task/saga/timeline IDs.
work_items.assessment: Typed scopes, definition/schema, native revisions, event/transition identities and provenance are defined without automatic conversion from saga/task/timeline coordinates.

work_items.requirement: Define feature matrix and `no_std` rules; explicitly choose whether HSM uses borrowed constant-size state paths or a caller-supplied workspace. Resolve const-generic capacity behavior and maximum nesting/depth budgets.
work_items.assessment: HSM uses bounded inline StatePath storage with const depth, cycle/depth refusal and no mandatory heap/runtime; hosted facade and portable core profiles are distinguished.

work_items.requirement: Write **compile-tested** small, hierarchical, legacy-saga-adapter and legacy-task-adapter public API fixtures before implementing everything.
work_items.assessment: Current flat/nested/prepared fixtures compile and run on stable/MSRV. This audit has not reconstructed whether every fixture was compile-tested before its implementation, as the plan requested.

work_items.requirement: Define machine protocol version 1 and a canonical byte encoding strategy that is deterministic, bounded and testable. Avoid conflating canonical encoding with default Serde JSON output from unrelated old protocols.
work_items.assessment: Independent Python-generated goldens, bounded versioned metadata and hosted canonical payload binding are implemented; old protocols retain separate versions.

phases.gate: A reviewer can trace the entire user request from event admission to candidate, commit, effect authorization, replay and diagnostics without finding two contradictory definitions of “accepted”, “committed” or “finalized”.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

phases.heading: F2 — Implement the portable machine core

work_items.requirement: Add `penelope-core/src/machine/*` modules and public `Machine`, `Transition`, `TransitionContext`, typed refusal/error, `IntentSink`, `PreparedTransition`, `MemoryMachine` (or a minimal wrapper in the correct layer).
work_items.assessment: Portable Machine, typed outcomes/errors, IntentSink and consuming MemoryMachine/PreparedTransition are implemented in existing core modules.

work_items.requirement: Implement deterministic state evaluation, staging, validation, rejection, safe publication and core provenance.
work_items.assessment: Preparation isolates candidate data and staging, validates before publication and publishes coherent state/head/provenance/intents. Callback purity remains a consumer obligation.

work_items.requirement: Keep flat-machine API allocation-free for allocation-free consumer types; require no `Clone` or serialization in base trait.
work_items.assessment: Base trait has no Clone/serialization bound; allocator probes cover flat/hierarchical allocation-free consumer types with positive controls.

work_items.requirement: Add state-path/HSM support with explicitly bounded depth and well-defined parent fallback/guard/entry/exit behavior; compile-test this against the target MSRV.
work_items.assessment: Bounded parent paths, terminal refusals, LCA hooks and internal/self behavior have explicit tests, independent tree/table oracles and stable/MSRV checks.

work_items.requirement: Use no mandatory async runtime, SQLite, saga, task or timeline dependency.
work_items.assessment: Core dependency manifest and enforced layering keep mandatory runtime/SQLite/saga/task-host/timeline dependencies out of portable machine evaluation.

work_items.requirement: Add a machine-specific `no_std` RISC-V build and allocation probe, not just a host `cargo check`.
work_items.assessment: Archived stable/MSRV RISC-V builds and machine-specific allocator probes cover the supported bare/serde profiles; no physical-board or arbitrary callback guarantee follows.

phases.required_tests: transition truth tables, attempted illegal edges, parent bubbling, guard refusal, panic safety, rejected staged-intent poison/drop, exhaustive depth, edge-specific state-local data, deterministic replay oracle and no-heap profile.
phases.gate: A user can build a flat and nested machine via the `penelope` facade alone; all state changes are explicit, testable, and do not depend on storage. Compiled examples are the published API, not aspirational pseudocode.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

phases.heading: F3 — Consolidate saga and graph into the unified model

work_items.requirement: Create canonical `penelope::saga` reexports and a machine-compatible saga projection/decision adapter.
work_items.assessment: Canonical saga namespace exposes native linear/graph preparation with common read-only decision inspection, retaining native state/provenance types.

work_items.requirement: Introduce shared private graph/provenance/validation helpers only after differential tests prove identical decisions and failure modes.
work_items.assessment: Preparation delegates to existing engines; common inspection and verified receipt helpers have multiple real callers. Graph protocol/evaluation authority is not replaced by an unnecessary universal graph engine.

work_items.requirement: Preserve legacy `LinearSagaEvent`, `GraphSagaEvent`, definition digests, step ordering, `ActionResult::Unknown`, compensation and manual review.
work_items.assessment: Frozen old saga observations cover statuses, compensation, retry/manual-review/unknown outcomes and replay through legacy and prepared paths; independent wire contracts remain unchanged.

work_items.requirement: Keep fast public functions available through compatibility reexports; do not introduce extra validation passes on the hottest step path unless measured and justified.
work_items.assessment: Legacy fast functions remain available and preparation delegates once. Measured selected saga profiles do not cross the review threshold, which does not prove universal latency equivalence or close the release performance gate.

work_items.requirement: Update trade, graph, compensation and retry examples to show how a saga is a specialized machine and how an application machine may coordinate with one.
work_items.assessment: Trade, compensation and retry use prepare_linear. The shared prepared_decisions example now includes graph preparation using the same inspection helper; durable consumer demonstrates application-machine/native-saga coordination.

phases.required_tests: generate identical legacy inputs/history under 0.4 and 0.5 and compare projections, next actions, statuses, errors, record bytes and replay (including graph limits/invalid edges/unknown effects).
phases.gate: Every previous saga supported case returns the same outcome with no wire changes, and the new facade composes sagas without introducing an alternate execution authority.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

phases.heading: F4 — Consolidate task supervision into the unified model

work_items.requirement: Provide machine-compatible task inspection/transition adapters and common provenance, with distinct `TaskStatus` and task effect results intact.
work_items.assessment: Task prepared record view implements shared inspection while native TaskStatus, record sequence and effect types retain their meanings.

work_items.requirement: Refactor duplicated candidate validation carefully; keep `TaskProjection::apply` atomic and `TaskControl`/`TaskSupervisor` recovery semantics unchanged.
work_items.assessment: One private isolated-candidate evaluator serves propose/apply/prepare. Frozen old projection comparisons and failure tests retain atomic application and native recovery boundaries.

work_items.requirement: Implement typed machine-intent-to-task launch and verified task-result-to-machine-event composition with explicit identity binding and idempotency.
work_items.assessment: Native receiver binds full machine source and host policy; protected consumer verifies actual task output before subsequent machine transition. Admission and source acknowledgement remain distinct.

work_items.requirement: Retain generation fencing, checkpoint migration proof, journal commit before execution, unknown-outcome reconciliation and protected worker profile.
work_items.assessment: Native TaskControl/Supervisor retain journal-first commands, generation/recovery fencing and ambiguity/poisoning. Protected workflow and audited negative tests exercise those boundaries.

work_items.requirement: Ensure the plain in-memory machine does not pull in task runtime dependencies.
work_items.assessment: Pure machine core has no task runtime dependency. The existing hosted facade is not claimed to be no_std.

phases.required_tests: existing portable task/SQLite worker fuzz, injected failures, real-thread arbitrations, stale generations, checkpoint corruption, poisoned supervisor, missing/ambiguous receipts and task-effect bridge.
phases.gate: All 0.4.0 task histories are still reconstructible and accepted only under the same conditions. A common machine interface cannot authorize a forbidden task retry or skip reconciliation.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

phases.heading: F5 — Integrate timeline without cloning its machinery

work_items.requirement: Add an adapter between user `Machine` transitions and `RewindableComputation` that preserves isolated scratch and staged intents.
work_items.assessment: MachineTimeline implements existing RewindableComputation with captured context, isolated candidate and staged effects; no second correction engine is introduced.

work_items.requirement: Reuse existing timeline instance ownership, `FixedHistory`, reservations, candidate validation, head CAS and effect finality.
work_items.assessment: Native LiveTimeline/history/reservations/replay/head/finality remain authoritative. Adapter storage/provenance wrappers preserve distinct native and timeline coordinates.

work_items.requirement: Add explicit tests distinguishing live canonical transitions from tentative timeline corrections and effect-finalized history.
work_items.assessment: Machine adapter tests distinguish native-memory state, live steps, corrected tentative effects and finalized handoff, including finalized-prefix refusal and failure isolation.

work_items.requirement: Document what happens when a machine definition/schema changes across a replay window, and when data dependencies cannot be captured.
work_items.assessment: Pinned definition/schema mismatch refuses correction. Documentation requires complete deterministic inputs and explains when mutable aliases or uncaptured dependencies make rewind ineligible.

work_items.requirement: Do not promise a persistent correction adapter as a side effect of adding machine SQLite persistence.
work_items.assessment: Docs explicitly separate in-memory timeline correction from durable machine snapshots; no persistent full-timeline recovery profile is claimed.

phases.required_tests: existing `penelope-timeline` property/fuzz campaigns plus hierarchy replay, invalid correction, missing predecessor, stale head, branch exhaustion, effect-finalized-prefix refusal and client prediction sample.
phases.gate: All 0.4.0 timeline examples remain valid, new machine examples can use the optional timeline, and the shared code is smaller/clearer than implementing another correction engine.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

phases.heading: F6 — Add machine durability and cross-subsystem effects

work_items.requirement: Add the independent machine event/provenance/intent protocol to `penelope-ports` and the core as appropriate to no-std separation.
work_items.assessment: Portable machine metadata and hosted payload/storage contracts use an independent protocol while retaining no_std separation.

work_items.requirement: Implement a bounded `MachineStore` and local `penelope-sqlite` adapter with a separately versioned migration, verified receipts, duplicate admission, competing CAS, loss-of-receipt reconstruction, scoped quotas and source-authorized outbox dispatch.
work_items.assessment: Authorized bounded journal/CAS, exact retries/receipts, snapshots, migrations, quotas and source-bound delivery are implemented and tested; final full-source chaos remains open.

work_items.requirement: Share existing SQLite worker, transaction, checksum, immutable blob, resource budgeting and lease helpers **by extraction**, not code duplication.
work_items.assessment: DatabaseWorker, byte/identity admission and verified receipt helpers are shared. Native transactions/leases remain separate for documented authority and protocol reasons; no blanket absence-of-duplication claim is made.

work_items.requirement: Add machine-to-saga and machine-to-task durable bridges using exact bound identities, committed outbox/intents and separately acknowledged downstream acceptance.
work_items.assessment: Native task/saga receivers bind exact committed source and their own acceptance evidence; source acknowledgement is separately fenced, not a cross-store transaction.

work_items.requirement: Provide a local-memory journal implementation for tests/examples only if useful; do not accidentally imply it is crash-durable.
work_items.assessment: Test-only journal peer checks preparation/CAS/receipt behavior and is explicitly not production crash-durable storage.

work_items.requirement: Preserve SQLite's single-host local-disk profile; no implied clustered durability or universal exactly-once delivery.
work_items.assessment: SQLite profile remains single-host WAL/FULL on supported local disk; neither clustered durability nor exactly-once external execution is inferred.

phases.required_tests: process-kill at precommit/postcommit/pre-receipt/pre-dispatch/post-dispatch stages; double writers; corrupted history; wrong tenant; duplicate event; concurrent reopen; unavailable history; quota exhaustion; old SQLite schema reopen/migration; async queue overflow and blocking I/O isolation.
phases.gate: An application-defined machine can crash and recover exact committed state plus pending authorized intents, and an ambiguous external effect never yields a guessed success or automatic unsafe restart.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

phases.heading: F7 — Refactor facade, docs, tests, performance and maintenance surface

work_items.requirement: Refactor facade into canonical namespaces; retain valid legacy reexports and all old examples/compile harnesses.
work_items.assessment: Canonical namespaces retain checked legacy exports; unchanged old consumer and current examples compile under their distinct dependency profiles.

work_items.requirement: Deduplicate verified internal validation/storage/diagnostic helpers. Remove unreachable compatibility **internals** only after tests prove they have no external behavior requirement; do not delete old wire decoding.
work_items.assessment: Verified shared owners replace repeated admission/candidate/worker/receipt plumbing. Legacy decoders and protocol-specific checks remain; no overall production LoC reduction is claimed.

work_items.requirement: Rework README to introduce: *machine -> optional durability -> saga/task effects -> optional timeline* in one example progression.
work_items.assessment: Short README starts with branch setup and canonical first-machine tutorial, then links optional durability/task/saga/timeline progression without duplicate model implementations.

work_items.requirement: Add one integrated example with model definition, invalid transition, durable commit, task/saga effect, ambiguous ACK, crash/recovery and provenance inspection.
work_items.assessment: Durable/protected consumer reuses one counter model, refuses overflow, restores state, inspects provenance, loses source acknowledgement, reopens/reclaims and verifies native worker output before later transition/saga admission. Reopen simulation and actual process-kill tests retain distinct scopes.

work_items.requirement: Add a comprehensive compatibility document and migration guide from 0.4.0.
work_items.assessment: Compatibility map covers API/protocol/native history and old-writer upgrade, with quiesced backup/copy validation and explicit backup-only rollback/reconciliation obligations.

work_items.requirement: Update architecture boundary checks and crate-package validation. Require new code paths to use canonical helpers instead of accruing further duplicate pathways.
work_items.assessment: Checkout-only architecture tests enforce layer/owner rules; all-ten clean archives and literal include checks pass at recorded revisions. The later example source is separately checked; final package identity reconciliation remains open.

work_items.requirement: Measure performance and maintenance cost before approving any “cleanup” that removes tested guarantees.
work_items.assessment: Maintenance/source/dependency/cost inventories and equivalent-work comparisons exist. Confirmed performance flags remain unresolved; shorter code or passing tests do not waive them.

phases.gate: An engineer unfamiliar with internals can use the whole framework through `penelope` docs; three specialized subsystems compose through one event/effect story; no legacy guarantee is lost.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

phases.heading: F8 — Release qualification and publication

work_items.requirement: Re-run full CI/qualification and compare against frozen 0.4.0 baseline using equivalent benchmark workloads.
work_items.assessment: Seven source CI jobs, source/package checks and equivalent-work comparisons pass in stated scopes; full immutable-source chaos and retained performance conclusions remain open.

work_items.requirement: Validate all crate packages on the exact release candidate, lockfile, MSRV, release build and external usage fixtures.
work_items.assessment: All-ten clean actual0.5 archives at ce93ff8 pass both compilers with696 reported passes each. Subsequent graph example has source-consumer qualification; final release package/source and release-build reconciliation is still required.

work_items.requirement: Review public API source compatibility, independently versioned machine wire goldens, old process/task/timeline protocol goldens and SQLite migrations.
work_items.assessment: Independent machine goldens, old wire/replay fixtures,14-profile static API review and actual old-writer database upgrade supplement scoped current tests.

work_items.requirement: Produce a release evidence manifest: commit SHA, tools, environment, seeds, run counts, failures, justifications and performance conclusions.
work_items.assessment: Revision-scoped manifests retain commands, hashes, tools, raw runs/failures and source scopes. One final release manifest cannot be completed before chaos and performance conclusions.

work_items.requirement: Only after explicit authorization, tag/publish `v0.5.0` using existing dependency-first scripts and release workflows. This plan does **not** authorize a release action.
work_items.assessment: No release tag or publication is authorized or performed. Dependency-first scripts and release contract describe the separately authorized final action.

phases.gate: The definition of done in section 14 is green on the actual release candidate, not just on an earlier feature branch.
phases.gate_disposition: Final qualification remains open; work-item support is scoped evidence, not a universal behavior or downstream-compatibility proof.

Verify section9.2 nested-example requirements, especially runnable hook tracing, self/parent transitions and guarded failures. Existing kernel tests are not by themselves a complete public-example demonstration.
Finish remaining detailed normative clauses outside section11 and reconcile them with the existing15-invariant, seven-maintenance-criterion and12-release-condition reviews.
